items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names state their purpose (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashRegexRewrite, CookieAttribute, deduplicateQueryParams, deduplicateFilterState). Every API field has a doc comment, and the code follows the existing trafficpolicy file layout.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Follows the plugin pattern: consistent_hash.go, wiring in constructor.go, applyConsistentHash, mergeConsistentHash. The log shows no codegen run (no make generate) and no applyconfigurations, so generated deepcopy/CRD files look hand-written. Separate dedup helpers per type repeat the same logic.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: API boundaries are validated with MinLength=1 on headerName, name, key and pattern, plus a CEL rule for disable. The patch is truncated, so regex and TTL parse errors can't be checked. Hidden F2P tests fail 0/2.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: mergeConsistentHash is registered and uses mergeOrigins.Append/SetOne("consistentHash") for union and p2-only inherit. Its own tests pass, but the union needed a fix commit and hidden F2P tests fail 0/2. Re-sort and sourceIp priority can't be confirmed.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: The CRD YAML has a CEL rule '!has(self.disable) || !self.disable || (!has(self.headers)...)'. The merge test 'higher_priority_disable=true_suppresses_lower_priority_policy' passes. The empty-spec default to sourceIp is said to be built in the IR.
